rows.description: A teenager who asks rhetorical questions like do you even care may be hurt, angry, sarcastic or making a point. Answering the feeling behind it works better than answering the literal words.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager may sound very certain to fit in, or hedge with maybe or I guess to avoid being wrong. Tone can hide real doubt, so a friend can ask what the teen would need to be sure.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager may hide surprise or confusion with a poker face or a joke in front of peers. A private check later helps sort out whether they really understood.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager challenges rules and disputes ideas to build independence and identity. It is normally a sign of growth, and adults can listen for the request underneath the challenge.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: In India a head wobble can mean yes, okay, I hear you or maybe, depending on context and tone. Listeners check with a clarifying question rather than assuming agreement or refusal.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager who demands may be frustrated, scared, or copying a tone heard elsewhere. Adults respond to the need under the demand and restate the request politely without giving in to the tone.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager invites friends or appeals to a parent for later curfew with reasons. Appeals with respectful tone and evidence more often succeed than pressure and threats.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager may hear advice from a parent as a lecture or control even when meant as care. Brief, respectful suggestions and asking what help is wanted improve how it lands.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager weighs recommendations from friends and influencers about trends, products and risks. Advice that carries pressure to do something unsafe or secret is a reason to consult a trusted adult.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager learns that saying yes once does not authorize everything, and that consent to share a picture or location can be withdrawn. Anyone who pressures or threatens is unsafe and should be reported.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26
